criterion.A5: Selected judge detection rate >= 0.90 for every perturbation type, pooled over the three pools, among segments where both base and perturbed judge outputs parse.
criterion.decision_update: Judge accepted only if A1-A3 pass, A4 is not failed, and A5 passes.
criterion.judge_selection_unchanged: Judge selection still uses T0/T1 only.

information_accessed_before_declaration: Human MQM and reward scores on the three already-opened pools (via the dry run). Judge jobs were running; no judge output file was read.
reason: An evaluator dry run with synthetic judges (real rewards, real human MQM) found zero reward x pool x rule cells with significantly negative human selection gain, so A4 (detecting reward selections that hurt humans) is untestable on WMT candidates: every candidate is a real MT system output. Generative RL can produce degenerate outputs that no WMT pool contains.
reported_not_gating: Detection rates of external QE rewards on the same items, as a description of which rewards are fooled by which degeneration.

test.T4_known_hack_detection: For each sampled segment, the best human-rated candidate (base) is degraded five ways: source_copy, truncation_half, appended_unrelated, unrelated_fluent, repetition. Donor text is the base of a different segment in the same pool (fixed cyclic shift). A judge or reward detects a perturbation on a segment when it scores the perturbed text strictly below the base. The judge's base score is taken from its T1-T3 validation output (same prompt, greedy decoding).
